The inline SWAR version costs 16174, about twice the 7570 of the `bits.OnesCount64` version. The interpreter seems to charge `bits.OnesCount64` as a single call, whereas the inlined SWAR code executes about 12 SSA instructions per word. I'm going back to the intrinsic and unrolling the loop by four to cut per-word loop overhead (compare, increment, branch). I haven't run it, so the saving is an estimate.
